title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
statement: You may change at most k characters of the string to any other letter. Return the length of the longest substring that could consist of a single repeated letter after those changes.

large_tests.gen_code:
import random
def gen():
    r = random.Random(13)
    return [''.join(r.choice('ABC') for _ in range(30000)), 1000]

hints.1_question: For a window, how many characters would you have to change to make it uniform? Which letter should you keep?
hints.2_nudge: Keep the count of the most frequent letter in the window. A window is valid when its length minus that count is at most k.
hints.3_big_hint: Grow right; update counts and the max count; while (window length - maxCount) > k: remove s[left], left += 1. Track the best length.

known_bugs.name: shrinks when changes needed equals k (>= instead of >)
known_bugs.followup: If you are allowed exactly k changes and the window needs exactly k, is it still valid?

known_bugs.name: forgets to decrement the count when the window shrinks
known_bugs.followup: When left moves past a character, should that character still count toward the window?

known_bugs.name: tries every start and rescans (O(n * window))
known_bugs.followup: For each start you restart counting from scratch. What work from the previous start can you reuse?

followups: Why is it fine that maxCount is never decreased when the window shrinks?
How would the solution change if you could only change letters to a specific target letter?
